display.description: Gilded Debt quest offer, reminder, and turn-in scene.
display.title: Gilded Debt

lines: Good. Some work only looks lighter after you pick it back up.
Are you sure you want me to put this quest aside?

abandoned: Then I will set this aside. Come back if the work still matters.
abandoned_cooldown: Then I will set this aside for a while. Let the trail cool before asking again.
abandoned_forever: Then this matter is closed. I will not reopen it.
unavailable: There is no active trail here for me to fold away.

lines: Then keep the work close until you are ready.
Gilded Debt is still open. I can repeat the details, or close my notes if you are done.

completed: Settled. The village gains relief, and a few whispers it will deserve. Some rewards are complicated.
inactive: The conditions for this quest are not right at the moment.
missing_objectives: The settlement still needs one gold block.
missing_proof: Gilded Blackstone is the proof. Without it, this is only an expensive apology.
missing_target: Do not hand me gold and call it courage. Reach the bastion first.
unavailable: This quest is not ready to close yet.

lines: Good. Maybe wisdom finally found a chair in this room.
An old debt has a gold edge and a bad smell. I need it settled once, cleanly.
There is a bastion tied to a ledger I wish did not exist. Bring proof and payment, or leave this alone.

inactive: The conditions for this quest are not right at the moment.
reminder: Bastion near {target_x}, {target_z}. Gilded Blackstone for proof, one gold block for settlement. No second ledger.
unavailable: That quest is not in your hands right now.

locate_failed: The bastion will not show itself. I refuse to chase a debt blind.
started: The bastion is {direction}, about {distance} blocks away, near {target_x}, {target_z}. Bring Gilded Blackstone and one gold block. If you abandon this, I close the matter for good.
unavailable: No. This ledger opens only for someone already trusted with sharp endings.

lines: If you brought that shine back, put it where I can see it and nowhere near my conscience.
Then hold onto it until you are ready to settle the matter.
